Trading disclosure
What happened?

Shares of online community and discussion platform Reddit (NYSE:RDDT) fell 25.2% in the morning session after the company reported third-quarter 2026 financial results and issued fourth-quarter guidance that fell below Wall Street's estimates.

According to a company press release, Reddit reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $895 million, up 53% year on year, and diluted earnings per share of $1.40. Both figures exceeded Wall Street expectations, topping consensus analyst estimates of $877.2 million in revenue and $1.33 in earnings per share. However, forward-looking guidance dampened investor sentiment. Reddit projected fourth-quarter 2026 revenue between $1 billion and $1.03 billion and adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization) between $480 million and $510 million. At the midpoints of $1.02 billion and $495 million, respectively, both revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance missed consensus estimates of $1.04 billion and $509.4 million. In addition, domestic daily active visitors fell by 900,000 year on year to 50.7 million, raising concerns over domestic user traction.

On the earnings call, CEO Steve Huffman attributed user softness to search referral traffic dropping by over 1 million weekly visits in October as Google expands AI Overviews, warning that fourth-quarter daily active uniques could drop by a low-double-digit percentage. Huffman noted that logged-in and mobile app users generate over 80% of monetization, prompting tests to shift toward a logged-in-only platform.

The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks. Is now the time to buy Reddit? Access our full analysis report here, it's free.

What is the market telling us

Reddit's shares are extremely volatile and have had 57 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for Reddit and indicate this news significantly impacted the market's perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 18 days ago when the stock dropped 3.6% on the news that rising benchmark Treasury yields and profit-taking across communication services pressured high-valuation growth equities ahead of key inflation data.

The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield climbed four basis points to 5.27%, lifting discount rates across long-duration equities. Communication services lagged the broader market with a 1.5% morning drop, as Reddit slid toward an intraday low of $151.42 after opening near $160.90.The decline halted a multi-day advance after Needham analyst Laura Martin reaffirmed a Buy rating and a $300 price target in research carried by Tipranks.

title: Reddit stock plunges 29.2% as Google AI cuts US traffic
detail:
Reddit stock plunges 29.2% as Google AI cuts US traffic
Todd Campbell
Sat, October 31, 2026 at 9:07 AM CDT 4 min read
RDDT
GOOG
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Updated to reflect Reddit closing stock price on 10/30/2026

Reddit's stock plunged 29.2% on Friday, October 30, after the company said its U.S. audience is shrinking due to Google's AI search features.

The sell-off came even though third-quarter revenue jumped 53% to $895 million. U.S. daily users fell to 50.7 million, down 2.5 million from the prior quarter, and CEO Steve Huffman said search referrals dropped by more than 1 million a week in October.

Shares, which closed at $129.60 on October 29, traded below their 52-week low of $119.27, changing hands at $91.73 at 4 pm EDT. For investors who bought Reddit as an AI winner, the message is that the same technology is now taking away the traffic that feeds the business.

Reddit is tied deeply to Google

Reddit runs the discussion forums where users post questions, advice and opinions, and it makes money mainly from advertising.

Much of its audience arrives from Google searches, which is why search changes matter so much. The stock has been popular with retail investors, but its data is also valuable to AI companies.

In 2024, Reddit inked deals with Google and OpenAI, allowing their respective Gemini and ChatGPT large language models to train on Reddit content in exchange for $60 million and $70 million per year, respectively.

Related: Googling for Reddit answers is about to get harder

Deals like that have supported revenue, but concern is that AI overviews are reducing traffic to Reddit by more than the company is pocketing from its AI deals.

Reddit reports "daily active uniques," or DAUq, split between logged-in users, who tend to be more engaged, and logged-out users, who often arrive from search and see fewer ads and less engagement. That split is the heart of today's drop.

In Q3, global DAUq rose 12% year-over-year to 130.3 million. However, U.S. DAUq fell 1% year-over-year, as a 4% dip in logged-out users overwhelmed a 1% increase in logged-in users.

"Google has really shifted in their relationship with the rest of the Internet," said CEO Steve Huffman on Reddit's earnings call. "People still want Reddit. It's just Google is not sending them to Reddit the way they used to."

Reddit CEO Steve Huffman saw a drop in logged-out user engagement as Google referrals fell due to AI overviews.Bloomberg / Getty Images
Reddit quarter was far from a disaster, but worries remain

Reddit revenue in the third quarter rose a more than healthy 53% to $895 million and while DAUq saw headwinds, U.S. revenue was still up 50% to $719 million.

As a result, Reddit's profit improved, with diluted EPS clocking in at $1.40, above Wall Street estimates of $1.33.

Reddit (NYSE:RDDT) plans to move to a mostly logged-in experience, limiting casual browsing for anonymous visitors.

The shift is aimed at deepening engagement, refining ad targeting and curbing AI scraping of Reddit discussion data.

The change has drawn investor pushback and regulatory attention over whether the risks were clearly flagged to shareholders.

Reddit runs a global discussion platform within the Interactive Media and Services industry, where logged-in communities, moderators and advertisers all rely on user accounts and identity signals to function. That setup makes any shift in sign in requirements especially important for how the business connects its US$24.9b social forum ecosystem with its ad partners.

How does a logged-in Reddit experience affect the business model?

A mostly signed-in user base gives Reddit cleaner identity signals, which helps the platform sell more targeted ads and support its AI tools. The trade off is that restricting anonymous browsing can trim casual traffic, so the ad engine leans harder on depth of engagement rather than headline user counts.

Does this change the Reddit Narrative around AI data licensing?

The move lines up with the Narrative view that Reddit's conversation data is valuable for AI and licensing deals, but also highlights a key risk. Tighter access strengthens Reddit's bargaining position on renewals, while uncertainty over long term AI data contracts and reliance on digital advertising stay firmly in focus.

What should Reddit investors watch next to judge if this works?

The next checkpoint is Reddit's Q4 2026 update, where management has guided revenue to US$1,000 million to US$1,030 million and flagged tests of logged-in only access outside the US. Key Takeaways

Reddit shares fell another 25% today after its third-quarter report, leaving the stock 63% below its January high.

B. Riley cut its price target on Reddit to $190 from $270 and kept its Buy rating, a target 95% above the current price.

Reddit's U.S. daily users fell 2% from a year earlier, and the company said its search referral traffic fell meaningfully during the quarter.

B. Riley's target needs only a below-average multiple, but it depends on earnings estimates that shrinking U.S. users and a Google renewal put at risk.

Reddit (RDDT:NYSE) grew revenue 53% in the third quarter, and the stock still fell another 25% today. It now sits 63% below its January high, and B. Riley still sees 95% upside.

The users are the problem

U.S. daily active uniques grew 6% in the second quarter of 2026, down from 51% in the third quarter of 2024.

The third quarter made it worse. U.S. daily users fell 2% from a year earlier to 50.7 million, and Reddit told shareholders: "Our search referral traffic was down meaningfully in Q3, with the decline accelerating later in the quarter."

Even the beat was smaller. Revenue of $895 million came in $25 million above the high end of guidance. In each of the three quarters before, the beat was $58 million to $80 million. Fourth-quarter revenue guidance of $1.00 billion to $1.03 billion also fell short of the $1.05 billion to $1.06 billion that analysts' full-year estimates implied.

B. Riley analyst Naved Khan cut his target to $190 from $270 today and kept his Buy rating.

B. Riley's path runs through earnings Reddit is already producing. Third-quarter net income was $283 million, 32% of revenue. At Thursday's close, analysts expected $8.54 a share over the next twelve months, so $190 works out to 22x those earnings.

title: Reddit: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
detail:
Reddit: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
The Motley Fool Team, The Motley Fool
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 3:07 PM CDT 3 min read
RDDT
Trade Reddit on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 29, 2026, Reddit (NYSE:RDDT) announced plans to test a logged-in-only user experience. The change aims to protect platform content from unauthorized data scraping. Long-term shareholders must watch whether this strategy converts casual search visitors into high-value daily app members. Three things management said stand out.

1. Requiring User Logins Protects Data and Improves Ad Targeting

External search engines are sending fewer visitors to the site, prompting management to push users toward logged-in accounts. Gated access protects community data from unauthorized scraping and provides advertisers with clearer signals to target audiences.

Moving to primarily logged-in will ensure our users have the best Reddit experience possible and can find the content and communities most relevant to them.
-- Steven Huffman, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer

2. App Personalization Is Driving Stronger First-Week User Retention

Converting casual web traffic into regular app users requires immediate relevance. Recent machine learning, or software that learns from data patterns to deliver better recommendations, has improved initial user retention significantly.

The percentage of new users who returned the first week after installing the Reddit app is up double digits quarter-over-quarter and over 50% year-over-year.
-- Steven Huffman, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer

3. Automated Ad Products Are Converting Intent Into Higher Revenue

Advertisers are paying higher rates for direct user engagement across performance campaigns. Upgraded machine learning models deliver faster user action, generating dramatic volume growth in ad clicks and buyer conversions.

In Q3, click volume grew over 50% and conversion volume more than tripled year-over-year.
-- Jennifer Wong, Chief Operating Officer

Looking Ahead

Reddit's user engagement is deepening across app feeds as the platform prioritizes direct habits over search traffic. High intent and proprietary user data provide strong advantages.

So as we look ahead, our strategy to make Reddit a direct daily habit for more people is simple: make Reddit awesome, grow community and belonging, and bring in new audiences.
-- Steven Huffman, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer

Commercial subreddits and software efficiency support pricing power. Strong cash flow provides flexibility for ambitious revenue targets.

Our next internal North Star is $5 billion in revenue, which will require strong execution to capitalize on the unique raw materials Reddit has.
-- Andrew Vollero, Chief Financial Officer

title: Reddit Stock Plunges 30% as Google's AI Search Hits Traffic and User Growth

Trading disclosure

Reddit shares plunged 30.44% to $90.15 on Friday after CEO Steve Huffman warned that Google's AI-powered search features are cutting referral traffic and could shrink the platform's user base.

The selloff came after the company reported strong third-quarter results but issued a weaker-than-expected revenue forecast for the current quarter.

Myriad: Where does ETH go next? Click to make your prediction.

Reddit built much of its business around people discovering its discussions through Google searches, and those visitors are increasingly finding answers without ever clicking through to the platform. That puts pressure on the advertising business that has helped turn Reddit into one of the internet's fastest-growing publicly traded companies.

Reddit's third-quarter numbers initially looked healthy. Revenue climbed 53% year over year to $895 million, advertising revenue increased 54% to $847 million, and net income reached $283 million. Diluted earnings per share, which measure company profit attributable to each share while accounting for potential dilution, came in at $1.40, up 75% from a year earlier and above the $1.33 analyst consensus.

But the audience figures were less encouraging since Reddit reported 130.3 million daily active unique visitors, up 12% year over year but below the roughly 134 million analysts expected. In the U.S., the number actually fell 2% to 50.7 million, giving investors another reason to question whether the platform can maintain its growth.

Huffman delivered the warning during Thursday's earnings call, explaining that Google search referrals had fallen by more than one million on average every week during October, with the decline accelerating toward the end of the third quarter. If that pace continues, Reddit's total daily active users could fall by a low double-digit percentage in Q4 from the current base of around 130 million.

Huffman pointed directly at Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode, features that generate answers and summaries directly inside search results. Rather than sending users to websites to find information, Google increasingly gives them what they are looking for on its own page, pushing traditional search links further down.

Asked whether the changes were responsible for Reddit's declining search traffic, Huffman said the AI features had expanded aggressively in the U.S. and internationally. "The AI mode does not drive traffic, not for us and not to anybody as far as I know," he told investors.

That creates an awkward situation for Reddit—and arguably every other single media site on the internet. People can still search for Reddit discussions, but Google's results increasingly allow them to consume information from those discussions without visiting Reddit itself. Search referrals also bring back existing users, meaning fewer clicks can affect both new-user acquisition and the platform's ability to keep people engaged.
